By David FelibaOctober 21, 2026 at 5:28 PM UTCBookmark
Save
Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
A rout in Argentina’s bonds has taken bullish investors by surprise, as a global emerging markets pullback compounds concerns over President Javier Milei’s reelection prospects and the country’s ability to meet billions in upcoming debt payments.
Argentina’s sovereign dollar bonds have been the worst performers across emerging markets over the past two months, with a relentless selloff pushing yields to nearly 12% earlier this week and spreads to their highest level in more than a year. The losses have accelerated despite calls from asset managers including Vontobel, Carmignac, Schroders and ProMeritum Investment Management, who have said the debt is too cheap to ignore.

item.title: Odd Lots: Why Politics Is Economists’ Blindspot
item.description:
Oct 21st, 2026
Odd Lots: Why Politics Is Economists’ Blindspot
Trade unions, rent stabilization and price controls — these are policies that conventional economics tells us capitalism would be better off without.
Professor James Robinson of the University of Chicago joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway to explain why he thinks economists need to consider politics to establish a more inclusive institution. They spoke on the Odd Lots podcast, recorded live at Chicago's City Winery.

A blockbuster earnings report from SpaceX spurred a rally in technology stocks, easing concerns over whether a global investment spree in artificial intelligence can prove sustainable.
Shares of the satellite, rocket and AI company surged 7%, with the gain also fueled by Elon Musk’s remarks endorsing the prospect of a merger with Tesla Inc. The electric-car maker and Meta Platforms Inc. will report results later Wednesday. Super Micro Computer Inc. jumped on solid preliminary figures. The Nasdaq 100 rose 1.3%. A gauge of chipmakers added 2.2%.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
SpaceX bonds weakened Wednesday after the company posted results that surpassed analysts’ estimates but also said it was investing aggressively, signaling more borrowing could be ahead.
Risk premiums for the aerospace and AI company climbed, following widening for the company’s credit derivatives earlier this week. Spreads on SpaceX’s 6.6% notes due in 2046 widened 0.09 percentage point to 2.64 percent points as of 12:35 p.m. New York time.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Owners of municipal bonds usually aren’t happy to see their holdings go into the red, but this year, they’re taking full advantage of negative returns in September and early October.
Bondholders are selling their weakened securities en masse, employing a popular strategy where the losses help to whittle down their tax bills. Then, they’re using muni exchange-traded funds to get back into a market where yields are at their highest levelsBloomberg Terminal
in decades.
